scope.implementation: Managed recursive node construction in scheduler-bound invocations reserves full physical backing and one conservative owner allowance before allocation; covers compiler-boxed closure environments and dependency-owner nodes
scope.commit: Successful construction transfers the reservation with its charged ownership registration; later same-invocation graph handoff reuses that registration
scope.rollback: Unpublished reservation guard refunds on allocation failure, cancellation or invalid/partially retained dependencies; node and dependency leases roll back independently
scope.compatibility: Unbound synchronous allocation behavior and recursive source/planner admission remain unchanged

coverage: Exact managed-node byte cap accepts while one byte less rejects before ownership publication

A second managed allocation fails when the first has exhausted the cap and preserves the first node and its reservation
Dependency-table capacity contributes to admission before dependency lookup
Cancellation immediately after reservation refunds before allocation without publishing a node
Invalid second dependency rolls back the previously retained first dependency and refunds the unpublished node while preserving existing owned storage

Exact successful construction/result peak accepts; one byte less rejects with Fault 2 and unchanged observer output in pools of one, two and four workers
Successful generated closures retain working captures after scheduler destruction; settlement clears recursive bytes and scheduler state
Existing deep/shared runtime ownership, graph-budget boundaries, cancellation, generated task/callable/error transport and ordinary worker regressions pass
